texts: In subdivided atrium, A, C, D and E are not true; only B, urgent repair in older patients with chronic symptoms, is.
Untreated, most infants with subdivided left atrium die, classically about three quarters, so fifty percent understates it.
Repair is done on cardiopulmonary bypass; circulatory arrest is needed only occasionally, in small infants, not in all.
In infants the small left atrium is reached through the right atrium and the atrial septum rather than by a left atrial approach.
In subdivided right atrium, an obstructing membrane is excised surgically; catheter disruption is not the preferred approach.
In the picture, the four peddlers are chased out and only the old breathless sailor is taken in.
Memory hook: four peddlers out, one old sailor in.
